page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r7.6xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 24 dedicated physical cores on an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at 2.7 GHz, with 1 thread per core. The instance is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates average performance across most compute and memory workloads. The single-core stress-ng CPU performance is 1843.79, while the multi-core score reaches 23250.96. Memory bandwidth tests show 1263.88 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 129.12 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. In database and key-value store operations, the instance handles 23.5 million Redis SET operations per second and scores 11538.47 on PassMark database operations. For language model workloads, it achieves a strong text generation speed of 283.7 tokens per second with a small 135M model, though performance drops to an average of 14.18 tokens per second with a medium 7B model.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.r7.6xlarge offers a dense memory profile relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for memory-intensive workloads that do not require local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration. The absence of bundled local storage means storage costs are decoupled, allowing for flexible network storage configurations. This instance is well-suited for enterprise databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, data processing pipelines, and moderate-scale web serving applications.
